solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Leave the City in the wet

indicators.note: the City is placed within the word for wet, so one piece sits in the other

parts.note: damp means wet
EC is the postcode area of the City of London

explanation.surface: Someone abandons the City of London on a rainy day.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, whose postcode begins EC.
explanation.definitionFit: To decamp is to depart suddenly, often secretly, so it is a synonym of leave.

clue.text: Old flue needs replacing, that's sad

indicators.note: the letters must be put back in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A homeowner glumly notes that the old chimney flue has to be replaced.
explanation.definitionFit: Doleful means mournful or sorrowful, a synonym of sad.

clue.text: Lincoln is such a city — see around it

definitions.text: Lincoln is such a city — see around it

parts.words: Lincoln is such a city — see around it
parts.note: Lincoln is a ... city, and a bishop's see is centred on the great church

explanation.surface: A tourist note about the English city of Lincoln.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is not 'look' but a bishop's diocese, which surrounds its principal church.
explanation.definitionFit: Lincoln has a famous minster church that makes it a bishop's seat.

clue.text: Miss that may be clapped on the cricket pitch

definitions.text: that may be clapped on the cricket pitch
definitions.meaning: an over in cricket bowled with no runs scored is applauded by fans

explanation.surface: A young woman is applauded at a cricket ground.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a maiden over is six balls bowled without conceding a run.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means an unmarried girl and also a runless over in cricket.

clue.text: Pointless massacre produces funny reaction

indicators.note: a compass point (south) is dropped from the word for massacre, leaving it without a point

parts.note: slaughter is a massacre

explanation.surface: A senseless massacre that strangely provokes amusement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pointless' looks like 'senseless' but means lose a compass point: S for south comes off the front.
explanation.definitionFit: The sound and response people make at a joke is a funny reaction.

clue.text: A pound's put on clerical wear

parts.note: lb is the abbreviation for a pound weight, and the 's is read as a plural, giving lbs

explanation.surface: A pound is added to the price of priests' vestments.
explanation.definitionFit: Long white linen vestments are worn by clergy at Mass, making them clerical garments.

clue.text: Be generous with some incriminating information

definitions.meaning: to hand something over freely, as a present
a telltale clue that betrays a secret

explanation.surface: Generously sharing evidence that implicates someone.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb phrase it means donate; as a noun it is a revealing telltale sign.

clue.text: Used by athletes, it helps to make a record

definitions.meaning: the oval running circuit athletes race on

definitions.text: it helps to make a record
definitions.meaning: a song is one of the pieces on an album

explanation.surface: Something athletes use to set a record time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record' suggests a sporting best, but it is a music album made of songs.
explanation.definitionFit: A running circuit and a single song on an album share the same word.

clue.text: King overjoyed when told

parts.note: R is the abbreviation of Rex, Latin for king
elated means overjoyed

explanation.surface: A king is thrilled when he hears the news.
explanation.definitionFit: Related, in the sense of narrated or recounted, means told.

clue.text: Allow to rest peacefully? Quite the opposite

definitions.text: Allow to rest peacefully? Quite the opposite

parts.words: Allow to rest peacefully? Quite the opposite
parts.note: allow is LET and rest in peace is RIP, yet together the phrase means to act without any restraint, the reverse of peaceful rest

explanation.surface: A plea to let someone rest in peace, immediately contradicted.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally the pieces are LET (allow) and RIP (rest in peace), but the idiom means unleash noise or energy.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to give free rein or go all out, the very opposite of quiet repose.

clue.text: Particularly the highest

definitions.meaning: the phrase means especially, more than anything
literally, over everything else, at the top

explanation.surface: A short note about what stands out most.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means especially, and taken literally it means positioned over every other thing.

clue.text: Loose garments provided by Mikonos resort

indicators.note: resort is read as re-sort, so the letters are sorted again into a new order

explanation.surface: A Greek holiday island supplies flowing clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' reads as a holiday place but is re-sort, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Traditional Japanese robes are wide-sleeved and loosely wrapped garments.

clue.text: Frantic if centre is moved

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone becomes frantic if the centre of something is relocated.
explanation.definitionFit: Frenetic and frantic are synonyms, both meaning wildly hurried and agitated.

clue.text: The noise of a fiddle

definitions.meaning: a swindle or scam, a fiddle in British slang

explanation.surface: The sound a violin makes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddle' is not the violin but British slang for a dishonest scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a loud din and a dishonest money-making scheme.

clue.text: Highest place in the church

parts.note: suggests a senior rank in the clergy, but means the tallest part of the building

explanation.surface: A query about the top rank in the church hierarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Highest place' suggests an archbishop's rank; it is the physical top of the building.
explanation.definitionFit: The tall pointed tower on a church rises above everything else in it.

clue.text: Fat boy runs inside

indicators.note: the abbreviation for runs goes within the word for boy

parts.note: a lad is a boy
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: An overweight boy is running about indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Lard is rendered pig fat used in cooking.

clue.text: This comes of ignoring established customs

definitions.text: This comes of ignoring established customs

parts.words: This comes of ignoring established customs
parts.note: customs here is the customs authority at the border, not traditions; goods slipped past it are smuggled

explanation.surface: A moral about what happens when people disregard traditions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Customs' suggests traditions but means the border authority collecting import duties.
explanation.definitionFit: Smuggled goods that bypass the duty officials at the border are illicit imports.

clue.text: Consequently how the product is expressed

definitions.meaning: in arithmetic a product is the outcome of multiplication, given as an outcome

explanation.surface: A remark about how goods are described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Product' suggests manufactured goods, but is the outcome of multiplying.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means therefore, and a product is stated as the outcome of a sum.

clue.text: Cyrus, one resolved to be the centre of attention

indicators.note: re-solved, so the letters are worked out again in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: King Cyrus, a determined figure, becomes the focus of every eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A cynosure is a person or thing that is the focus of admiration, originally the pole star.

clue.text: Standard requirement for pirates?

parts.note: standard means a flag rather than something normal, and the pirate flag is the skull and crossbones

explanation.surface: A question about what pirates normally need.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard' reads as 'basic', but it is a flag or banner.
explanation.definitionFit: The skull-and-crossbones flag flown by pirate ships carries this traditional name.

clue.text: Fool sailor on a ship

parts.note: a jack, or jack tar, is a sailor
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A silly sailor aboard a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A jackass is a male donkey and figuratively a stupid person.

clue.text: Complain when I get involved with the law

indicators.note: involved suggests the letters are tangled together into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles when they end up in a legal dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: To wail is to cry out or lament loudly, a form of complaining.

clue.text: A welder renovating the sheltered side of a ship

definitions.text: the sheltered side of a ship

indicators.note: renovating means remaking, so the letters are rebuilt in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A welder at work repairing the hull of a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The side of a vessel facing away from the wind is the protected one.

clue.text: Draw ten out — of diamonds?

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of ten are knocked out of order

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A card player draws the ten of diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' looks like taking a card but is the definition, meaning attract.
explanation.definitionFit: To entice someone is to lure or attract them, to draw them in.

clue.text: Too inexperienced to express pain

parts.note: to call out is to express or voice something
ow is the cry of pain

explanation.surface: Someone too green to even voice their hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'express pain' is to call out 'ow!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Callow describes youthful immaturity and lack of worldly experience.

clue.text: One between the Left and the Right is unlikely to join a party

indicators.note: the word for one sits between the two side letters

parts.note: L stands for left
R stands for right
taken as the word itself

explanation.surface: A centrist politician, between left and right, refusing to join any party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' suggests politics but simply means a social gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A solitary person who keeps to themselves is unlikely to go to gatherings.

clue.text: What Nelson turned to his advantage at Trafalgar?

definitions.text: What Nelson turned to his advantage at Trafalgar?

parts.words: What Nelson turned to his advantage at Trafalgar?
parts.note: Nelson famously put his telescope to his sightless eye to ignore a signal, giving us the idiom turn a ___ to

explanation.surface: A history question about the admiral's tactics.
explanation.walkthrough: The anecdote is actually from Copenhagen (1801), not Trafalgar; the clue plays on the idiom 'turn a blind eye'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelson lost the sight of one eye, and deliberately ignoring something is named after his trick.

clue.text: An image of swindler admitting his crime?

definitions.meaning: a confidence trickster confessing might say ...

explanation.surface: A picture of a fraudster confessing.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it as I CON: what a con man admitting it would say.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacred painting or a representative symbol is an image.

clue.text: Tell everyone girl's gained weight

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name; the 's is a link meaning has
an ounce is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A girl tells everyone she has put on weight.
explanation.definitionFit: To announce something is to proclaim it publicly, telling everyone.

clue.text: Clasp one's leg-bone

definitions.meaning: a Roman brooch or pin fastening garments was called this
the outer, thinner bone of the lower leg

explanation.surface: Someone grips their own leg.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word for a brooch also names the slender outer bone of the shin, shaped like a pin.

clue.text: They may make nurses go out with them — to the theatre?

definitions.text: They may make nurses go out with them — to the theatre?

indicators.note: out signals the letters are thrown out of their usual order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Doctors who take nurses on dates to see a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Theatre' suggests a play but is the operating theatre, where surgeons lead the nurses.
explanation.definitionFit: Operating doctors take nursing staff with them into the operating theatre.

clue.text: Expert in Judo beaten

definitions.meaning: a skilled judoka has earned a coloured belt, a black belt for experts

explanation.surface: A judo master is defeated.
explanation.definitionFit: Having been awarded a grade belt marks a martial-arts expert, and being belted also means being struck.
